_about: Delivery-format presets. The DELIVERY format is a client x platform decision and belongs in clients/<brand>.md section 5 — this file is the shared vocabulary those profiles name, and the presets export_qc.py and slop_check.py read via --format. Nothing here is a default: a skill that assumes an aspect ratio produces confidently wrong work for every client that isn't vertical short-form.
_generation_note: GENERATION resolution is a separate decision from delivery resolution and is stack-dependent — see references/delivery-format.md section 4. Some stacks require generating at exactly the delivery size because a reference at another size returns the wrong shape; others are cheaper generating below delivery and upscaling once.
_verify: Safe-zone figures for the 9:16 presets are now MEASURED from platform-owned template files and carry their source and date; every other preset's margins remain approximate house values. Platform UI drifts and the template files are versioned — re-download rather than trusting a cached measurement. Resolution and fps are stable; loudness is a house convention (see loudness_note), not a spec.
_max_mb_note: OPTIONAL per preset (2026-11-03): "max_mb": <number>, the delivery's file-size ceiling in megabytes (1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes, the stricter reading of a ceiling written in MB). Add it only when a delivery names a ceiling; no preset carries one, and there is no default. export_qc.py --format reads it (or --max-mb gives it for one run) and FAILs a file above it, naming the size and the cap; the fix is to lower the target bitrate until the estimate fits, re-export, and record that the file compresses harder.

vertical-1080.label: Vertical short-form 9:16 1080p
vertical-1080.safe_zone_note: Both published files are AD safe zones — they budget for caption text, the CTA button and the profile row. Neither TikTok nor YouTube publishes anything for ORGANIC posts, and Meta publishes nothing retrievable for Reels at all: its own page facebook.com/business/help/980593475366490 is the arbiter and has to be opened in a browser. So: safe_zone_pct is the conservative evidenced box and is what anything that will run paid — or that carries a DISCLOSURE — must sit inside. safe_zone_organic_pct is the looser house convention for organic-only posting and has NO platform source; it is what this file carried for every preset until 2026-09-08, when the template files were measured and the bottom margin turned out to be understated by ~15 points. ⛔ The widely quoted Meta '14% top / 20% bottom' and the newer '14/35/6' both trace to blogs that cite no Meta URL. Do not use them.
vertical-1080.safe_zone_source: MEASURED 2026-09-08 from the platforms' OWN safe-zone template files, not from a spec listicle. TikTok: the In-Feed Standard PNG inside the ZIP linked from ads.tiktok.com/help/article/tiktok-auction-in-feed-ads (page updated June 2026; file dated 2025-04-15), authored on a 720x1280 grid -> top 12.5%, bottom 34.4%, sides 11.1%, widening to 27.8% on the right where the action rail sits. YouTube: the safe-zone SVG referenced by support.google.com/google-ads/answer/9128498, labelled 1080x1920 -> top 288px (15.0%), bottom 672px (35.0%), left 48px (4.4%), right 192px (17.8%). The values below are the MAX of each margin across those two, i.e. the box evidenced to survive both.
vertical-1080.loudness_note: HOUSE CONVENTION, NOT A PLATFORM SPEC. None of TikTok, YouTube, Facebook or Instagram publishes a loudness target for uploads; -14 LUFS migrated into social spec sheets from music streaming. The only loudness figure any of these companies publishes is Google's -24 LKFS for Display & Video 360, a different product. Keep -14 as a consistent mastering target across a batch — that consistency is the real value — but never quote it to a client as a platform requirement.
vertical-1080.audio_note: 48 kHz IS documented, by YouTube, Facebook and Instagram; Instagram states 48 kHz as a MAXIMUM, so a 96 kHz master is out of spec there. AAC-LC, stereo, 128 kbps+ is the documented intersection.

feed-4x5.label: In-feed portrait 4:5
feed-4x5.safe_zone_note: Feed placements crop less aggressively than Reels but still overlay a caption block below.

landscape-1080.label: Landscape 16:9 1080p
landscape-1080.safe_zone_note: Bottom margin leaves room for a player scrubber and burnt-in captions.

broadcast-eu-1080.label: EU broadcast 16:9 1080i/p 25fps
broadcast-eu-1080.loudness_spec_note: EBU R 128: -23 LUFS integrated, +/-0.5 LU for file-based programmes, -1 dBTP. EBU R 128 s1 (short-form, e.g. ads): short-term loudness never above -18 LUFS. export_qc.py enforces all three from this preset (v2.60.0).
broadcast-eu-1080.loudness_note: EBU R128: -23 LUFS, NOT the -14 streaming target. Delivering a -14 master to a broadcaster is a rejected deliverable, and it is the single most common format mistake when a social-first team is asked for a TV cut.

stills.label: Still images — website / marketing (Mode S, the stills lane)
stills._note: No fixed aspect, size or fps: a stills job delivers several shapes (a 16:9 hero, a 1:1 card, a 4:5 feed image), so each 01-script/prompts/<ID>.frame.prompt.md declares its own `aspect:` and gate.py holds the call to THAT. Valid only with `Mode: S` in the checkpoint, and Mode S is valid only with this preset (gate.py Job.validate). Not a video preset: export_qc.py, slop_check.py and build_captions.py have nothing to measure here.

_audio_note: 48 kHz is the video world's sample rate; 44.1 kHz is the music world's. A 44.1k library track dropped into a 48k timeline is the classic pitch/sync bug, and it is silent until someone hears it. Every preset states the rate so export_qc.py can check the rendered file rather than trusting the NLE.
